SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient reports onset of low back pain on 06/18/2026. She describes diffuse lumbar discomfort worsening with flexion.
Exam: Lumbar spine shows tenderness paraspinally, limited forward flexion. Neurologic exam reveals diminished ankle reflex bilaterally; strength is 5/5 elsewhere.
Assessment: Acute lumbar radiculopathy, likely L5/S1.
Plan: Start NSAIDs today (06/19/2026) for pain control. Initiate physical therapy beginning 06/22/2026. Advise activity modification. Return in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient returns for follow‑up after completing prescribed therapies. She reports ongoing low back pain.
Exam: Lumbar paraspinal tenderness persists. Neurologic exam shows diminished ankle reflex; strength 5/5.
Assessment: Chronic lumbar radiculopathy with incomplete response to conservative care.
Plan: NSAIDs were started on 06/19/2026 and continued through 07/27/2026 with partial relief. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/22/2026, consisting of 10 sessions, and concluded on 07/27/2026 without improvement. She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, or bowel/bladder symptoms. Objective neurologic examination reveals diminished ankle reflex consistent with L5/S1 radiculopathy. MRI to localize the level before a planned L4-L5 epidural steroid injection.
